name: Ropinirole
route_note: Oral immediate-release and prolonged-release tablets; a transdermal patch is marketed in Japan.

discovery.note: A non-ergoline indolone dopamine agonist developed for Parkinson's disease.

tagline: Dopamine agonist that was the first FDA-approved drug for restless legs syndrome
summary: Ropinirole is a non-ergoline D2/D3 dopamine agonist used to treat Parkinson's disease and restless legs syndrome. It was developed by SmithKline Beecham and is now widely available as a generic.
mechanism: Ropinirole is a full agonist at D2 and D3 dopamine receptors with little activity at D1, serotonergic or adrenergic receptors. Stimulation of striatal D2 receptors substitutes for lost dopaminergic input in Parkinson's disease.
In restless legs syndrome, low evening doses are thought to act on spinal and diencephalic dopaminergic pathways that modulate sensory symptoms.
uses: Parkinson's disease (monotherapy or adjunct to levodopa)

history.title: First launch
history.detail: Ropinirole (Requip) is launched in the UK for Parkinson's disease.

history.title: US approval
history.detail: The FDA approves Requip for Parkinson's disease.

history.title: 056 study
history.detail: A five-year trial reports fewer dyskinesias with initial ropinirole than with levodopa (Rascol et al., NEJM).

history.title: Restless legs syndrome
history.detail: Ropinirole becomes the first drug approved by the FDA for restless legs syndrome.

history.title: Extended release
history.detail: Once-daily Requip XL is approved in the US.

history.title: Generics
history.detail: Generic ropinirole tablets become available in the US.

pk.metabolism: hepatic, mainly CYP1A2 (ciprofloxacin and smoking alter levels)

facts: Ropinirole was the first medicine approved by the US FDA specifically for restless legs syndrome (2005).
